question: What is the primary goal of safe drug administration?

options.A: Reducing the cost of hospital pharmacy supplies
options.B: Speeding up the discharge process for patients
options.C: Ensuring correct treatment reaches the patient safely

explanation: Safety protocols aim to deliver the correct medication parameters to prevent patient harm. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why is medication administration considered a high-risk nursing duty?

options.A: Drugs are expensive to purchase in Nigeria
options.B: Patients always question their prescribed medicines
options.C: Errors can cause severe harm or death
options.D: Pharmacy departments rarely check doctor orders

explanation: Because drugs have potent physiological effects, mistakes directly threaten patient safety and clinical outcomes. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why must a nurse adhere strictly to the prescribed administration time?

options.A: To prevent the pharmacy from auditing drug stocks
options.B: To finish the ward round shift duties quickly
options.C: To maintain steady therapeutic drug levels in the blood
options.D: To ensure the doctor signs the chart on time

explanation: Giving medications on schedule keeps the drug concentration within the effective therapeutic range. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h2)

question: When should a nurse chart that a medication has been given?

options.A: Immediately after the patient swallows the drug
options.B: At the end of the entire morning shift
options.C: Before entering the patient ward cubicle
options.D: Before preparing the drug at the medication trolley

explanation: Documentation must follow administration instantly to prevent accidental double-dosing or omissions. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the clinical purpose of the Right Assessment principle?

options.A: Checking if the doctor wrote legible handwriting
options.B: Assessing how well the pharmacy stores drugs
options.C: Determining if the drug is safe to give right now
options.D: Calculating the total cost of the hospital bill

explanation: Baseline checks ensure current patient vitals or lab results do not contraindicate the planned medication dose. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h3)

question: What action defines the Right to Education during drug administration?

options.A: Teaching student nurses how to calculate drug dosages
options.B: Listing the cost of drugs on the patient bedside chart
options.C: Explaining the drug purpose and side effects to the patient
options.D: Reading the hospital pharmacy manual to the doctor

explanation: Patients must understand their treatment regimen to actively participate in their own healthcare recovery. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h4)

question: How should a nurse respond when a competent patient exercises their right to refuse a drug?

options.A: Document the refusal and notify the prescribing physician
options.B: Hide the crushed medication inside the patient's food
options.C: Scold the patient for failing to follow medical advice
options.D: Force the patient to swallow the medication immediately

explanation: Competent adults can refuse treatment; the nurse must report this safely rather than forcing compliance. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which identifiers are acceptable for checking a patient identity safely?

options.A: Diagnosis name and treating doctor title
options.B: Tribe of origin and language spoken
options.C: Full name and hospital identification number
options.D: Ward bed number and hospital room color

explanation: Unique identifiers like names and hospital numbers remain constant even if a patient changes beds. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h5)

question: A nurse enters a busy ward and notices a patient has been moved to a new bed. What must the nurse do?

options.A: Administer the medication based on the new bed number
options.B: Skip the dose until the patient returns to the original bed
options.C: Check the ID band against the MAR before giving drugs
options.D: Ask the ward cleaner to confirm the patient identity

explanation: Bed numbers change frequently, so nurses must rely on permanent identification bands and records. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why are quiet zones established during medication preparation in the ward?

options.A: To allow nurses to sleep during their busy morning shifts
options.B: To prevent patients from asking questions about their care
options.C: To reduce the noise level for doctors writing case notes
options.D: To minimize distractions and prevent calculation or selection mistakes

explanation: Concentration is vital when preparing drugs; interruptions are a major root cause of medication errors. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the immediate priority when a medication error is discovered?

options.A: Hide the medication bottle to avoid ward punishment
options.B: Assess the patient clinical condition and ensure safety
options.C: Blame the junior student nurse on duty
options.D: Wait until the end of the month to report the incident

explanation: Patient welfare always comes first; monitoring for adverse effects takes precedence over administrative reporting. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why is the nurse considered the final safeguard in drug administration?

options.A: Doctors never make mistakes when calculating dosages
options.B: Pharmacy departments do not check prescriptions in Nigeria
options.C: They are the last healthcare professional to interact with the drug before the patient
options.D: They are legally responsible for manufacturing all hospital drugs

explanation: As the person administering the drug, the nurse has the final opportunity to catch errors made by prescribers or pharmacists. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h7)

question: Which professional attitude is essential for a nurse working in a resource-constrained setting?

options.A: Delegating all drug preparation tasks to patients
options.C: Total reliance on verbal orders without documentation
options.D: Heightened vigilance and strict adherence to safety rights

explanation: Challenging environments require extra diligence to prevent systemic faults from harming patients. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h7)
